◀️Подборка из 5 уязвимости по CISA KEV за 20–25 ноября▶️

1. VMware vCenter (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8, KEV с 20.11)
В РФ и СНГ vCenter держит основную часть корпоративной виртуализации, при этом на 7.x/8.x часто нет поддержки Broadcom. При доступе к vmdird (TCP 2012) и знании SSO-учётки (administrator@vsphere.local) атакующий через предсказуемые UUIDv1 в DCE/RPC забирает сессионный ключ SRP-6a без пароля, скачивает data.mdb с ключом STS SAML, подписывает токен Global Admin и при доступе к 443/22 выходит в root. ARMORY CASTLE эксплуатировала баг с сентября утилитой BONESAW (Google GTIG), а 24 ноября Rapid7 воспроизвела цепочку. По VMSA-2026-0009 обхода нет: ставьте 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200, 9.1.1.0200 или 5.2.5 (для 7.0 патч только по расширенному контракту), закрывайте 2012/443/22 в сегменте управления и проверьте SSO на лишние учётки.

2. Drupal Core (CVE-2026-132165, KEV с 24.11 + CVE-2026-136716, активные атаки)
Массовая CMS на внешних порталах. Обе дыры бьют в открытый install.php: SA-CORE-2026-017 (CVE-2026-132165, атаки с 19.11) даёт захват сайта и RCE, а 25 ноября вышел SA-CORE-2026-019 (CVE-2026-136716, 21/25), потому что сайты в незавершённом состоянии установки остались под атаками и после первого патча. Обновитесь до 10.6.23, 11.3.23 или 11.4.14, запустите update.php, закройте install.php на веб-сервере и проверьте почту и логи user 1.

3. Cacti Core 1.2.31 (4HTTP2ROOT, 0-day вне KEV, PoC от 26.11)
В KEV бага нет, атак на 27.11 watchTowr не видел, но патча и CVE до сих пор нет. Cacti широко стоит у провайдеров и сетевых админов в СНГ и хранит SNMP-креды железок. С включённым гостевым доступом PoC бьёт за четыре HTTP-запроса: SQL-инъекция в preview_graphs_per_page уходит в LIMIT (graph_view.php), множественный запрос PDO меняет poller_item.arg1, а graph_realtime.php отдаёт строку в popen() от имени веб-сервера или поллера (обычно без root). Выключите гостя, спрячьте панель за VPN и проверьте settings_user и poller_item.

4. Vates Xen Orchestra (CVE-2026-133469, KEV с 25.11)
Популярная в СНГ замена VMware и самый простой эксплойт недели: один запрос с authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D парсится в {}, заставляет Redis отдать первый живой токен вплоть до админа и ведёт к root на XCP-ng (VSA-2026-062). Атаки идут: обновитесь до 6.9.2 / 6.10.1, уберите XO из интернета и проверьте хосты на VM pivot2, /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar2, /.ustar5 и трафик к 91.211.251.112.

5. Точечный периметр: Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver и Juniper Session Smart
Все три в KEV, но в РФ/СНГ встречаются реже. В кластерах Cisco Expressway до X15.5.20 (CVE-2026-76466, CVSS 9.8) статические куки и обход проверки сертификатов дают RCE от root (Cisco). В SAP NetWeaver Portal 7.50 (CVE-2025-42884, CVSS 6.5) атакуют неаутентифицированную JNDI-инъекцию (SAP 3660969). В Juniper Session Smart до 7.0.5/7.1.7/7.2.3 (CVE-2026-103406, CVSS 9.8) поддельный salt minion ID даёт команды от root без пароля (Juniper). У Cisco и Juniper обхода нет — при наличии на периметре патчите сразу.

Current active high-impact cybersecurity incidents and exploited vulnerabilities (forensic overview as of 27 November 2026)

This is a factual, open-source summary drawn from CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, vendor advisories, and confirmed public reports. It focuses on the most intensive and foundationally problematic items with active exploitation, widespread exposure, or high real-world impact right now. 
It is not a complete list of every minor issue.
 
The goal is practical awareness: many of these have known fixes or clear interim steps. 
Delayed patching, exposed management interfaces, and unpatched edge devices remain the common themes. 
Cross-checking your own systems (web servers, collaboration tools, network gear, mapping services, and any public-facing or management interfaces) against these reports regularly remains the proactive path.

Official sources are linked directly after each item.

CISA’s live KEV catalog is the authoritative U.S. list of vulnerabilities with reliable evidence of active exploitation: 
https://t.co/sRSfmZacaP

1. Drupal core installer-related site takeover (CVE-2026-136716, related to CVE-2026-132165)
Incident: 
Drupal sites in unusual or incomplete install states (including some production sites) remain open to unauthenticated site takeover even after an earlier November fix. Attackers can reinstall or fully control the site if `/core/install.php` is reachable. The vulnerable state is not obvious in the UI, and already-compromised sites may no longer look vulnerable. Drupal confirmed active exploitation in the wild. CISA added related entries to the KEV catalog.

Impact: 
Full site control, data theft, or use as a foothold. Affects supported Drupal 10.6 and 11.3/11.4 branches if not updated and the installer is not secured.

Source: 
https://t.co/WH2U0Kcp3N

Mitigation: 
Update to Drupal 10.6.23, 11.3.23, or 11.4.14 (or later), then run `update.php` (or equivalent). Strongly recommended: block or secure `/core/install.php` per Drupal’s installer-securing guidance (web-server config preferred; verify with curl that it returns 403/404). Check logs for unexpected user-1 activity and reset the user-1 password if needed. Drupal Steward provides some protection against known vectors but is not a substitute for the update. End-of-life branches have no fix, migrate.  
Official advisory and securing guidance are in the same Drupal link above. CISA KEV entry notes forensic triage.

2. Mitel MiCollab Audio/Web/Video (AWV) unauthenticated flaws, including CVSS 10.0 command injection (CVE-2026-133323 and related: CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133311, CVE-2026-133324)
Incident:
Five vulnerabilities in the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab (through 10.3 / 10.3.0.18) allow unauthenticated attackers to upload dangerous files, inject XML or commands, bypass checks, and run system commands. The lead issue is a blind OS command injection rated CVSS 10.0. Mitel noted that combining them amplifies impact. CISA added all five to the KEV catalog on 25 November 2026 after evidence of exploitation; short federal remediation deadlines apply (most 28 November).

Impact: 
Remote code execution / system control on affected MiCollab servers. Relevant to organizations using MiCollab for business communications.

Source:
Mitel advisory MISA-2026-0012: https://t.co/BHTDnYehYY  

CISA alert: 
https://t.co/ihJMiWBQm0

Mitigation:
Apply Mitel’s recommended updates/patches per the advisory. Restrict external access to the AWV component. Perform forensic triage for signs of command execution or unauthorized activity (CISA requires this for federal systems). Isolate if patching is delayed.

3. GeoServer unauthenticated file-read / authorization-bypass issues that chain toward higher impact (CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129243, and related chain including CVE-2026-129245)
Incident: 
GeoServer (open-source mapping/GIS server) has flaws allowing unauthenticated XML injection for local file reads or SSRF, plus an authorization bypass via a prefixed service name. Researchers demonstrated chains that can reach administrator session forgery and remote code execution. watchTowr reported probing/exploitation activity against the file-read and bypass issues. CISA added the key ones to KEV on 27 November 2026. Fixed versions were released earlier (October) and details published mid-November.

Impact:
Data exposure (including config and credentials), potential full compromise of exposed GeoServer instances. Common in government, utility, and mapping deployments.

Source: 
https://t.co/s4Xy0bFX4r

Mitigation:
Upgrade to GeoServer 3.0.2, 2.28.6, or 2.27.7 (or later matching your series). After upgrade, rotate administrator credentials and review for signs of stored-query creation or unauthorized access. Restrict exposure of the service. No simple workaround fully replaces the update for the chain.

4. Juniper Session Smart Conductor unauthenticated root command injection (CVE-2026-103406)
Incident:
In the AutomatedProvisioner component, a crafted Salt minion ID lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands as root. Juniper reported at least one malicious exploitation to its SIRT and updated its advisory. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 25 November 2026 (federal due 28 November) with forensic-triage guidance. The fix shipped in late October.

Impact:
Full root control of the Conductor management system, which can affect all Session Smart Routers it manages. Relevant to SD-WAN / network management deployments.

Source / advisory:
Juniper JSA112183 (support portal): search “2026-10 On-Demand Security Bulletin Session Smart Router and Session Smart Conductor” or the CVE record.  
NVD/CISA reference: https://t.co/sPApv1J78P

Mitigation:
Upgrade Session Smart Conductor (and related Routers) to 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3, or later. Juniper lists no workaround. Restrict management access and check for unexpected activity.

5. Optimizely Web Experimentation supply-chain script injection (CVE-2026-132224 / OPTIMJACK campaign)
Incident:
A flaw in the account signup flow allowed attacker-controlled JavaScript to be injected into Project JavaScript fields served from Optimizely’s CDN. This was actively used to deliver card-skimming, cryptocurrency address-swapping, cookie theft, and related payloads to visitors of affected customer sites (reported on ~178 organizations). Optimizely fixed the issue and cleaned the code; CISA added the CVE to KEV on 24 November 2026.

Impact: 
Browser-side theft of payment data, crypto, and session material from visitors of sites that loaded the affected Optimizely snippets. Classic supply-chain style delivery from a trusted CDN.

Source:
Optimizely status/incident report (linked from CISA notes): https://t.co/MPKuwGF7gY 
and the associated PDF security incident report. Analysis of the campaign appears in multiple independent reports (e.g., Ostorlab).

Mitigation:
Optimizely applied the fix and removed the injected code. Affected customers should review their Project JavaScript, revoke/reset relevant sessions and tokens, and confirm no residual malicious code remains. Monitor for related phishing or unexpected activity. Hosted service, patching is on the vendor side, but verification is on the customer side.

6. 1Password backend incident (employee GitHub account compromise)
Incident:
On/around 19 November 2026 an attacker accessed an employee’s corporate GitHub account, reached source code and CI/CD, and pushed malicious code that downloaded administrative account records for a subset of users (names, emails, account identifiers, timestamps, public keys, SRP parameters, certain invitation/recovery tokens, and other non-secret metadata). Vault contents, vault-protecting keys, account passwords, and Secret Keys were not accessed. 1Password confirmed containment actions and that services/availability/product security were not impacted.

Impact:
Potential for targeted phishing using the stolen metadata. Vaults remain secure.

Source:
Official statement: https://t.co/o1Zls1eQWn

Mitigation / customer advice:
Be wary of unexpected emails, texts, or calls claiming to be from 1Password about invitations or recovery. 1Password will never ask for your account password or Secret Key, enter those only in the official app or website you opened yourself. Codes in invitation/recovery emails were lengthened. Report suspicious activity to support@1password.com. No action needed for vault contents.

7. SAP security incident (reported GitHub / development-environment activity; internal codename Project Granite)
Incident:
SAP confirmed it identified suspicious activity and took protective measures. Media reports (citing internal communications and sources) describe activity on SAP’s GitHub development environment involving stolen employee authentication tokens that allowed copying and alteration of source code. SAP states that, based on its investigation to date, there is no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data. Signing keys were reportedly rotated and automated development processes restricted as part of the response.

Impact:
Potential supply-chain or integrity concerns for SAP software if modified code had propagated (not confirmed by SAP). Customer business data not indicated as affected so far.

Source:
SAP statements to media (e.g., SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, The Record) and contemporaneous reporting. No detailed public SAP Trust Center advisory was located in the immediate reports.

Mitigation:
Follow any guidance SAP issues to customers. Organizations running SAP should apply normal patch hygiene and monitor for unexpected behavior. No specific public customer-side CVE or mitigation package was detailed in the initial confirmations.

8. Reported breach of U.S. Air Force Cloud One platform
Incident:
Reuters (27 November 2026, citing multiple sources) reported that hackers breached the Air Force’s flagship Cloud One cloud computing platform. The intrusion was discovered within roughly the past month during upgrade work. Scope, attacker identity, and whether data was stolen remain unclear in public reporting. Sources described possible access via a software vulnerability to the control plane (management layer). The discovery has led to operational disruptions, including paused migrations of back-office applications and blocked updates on existing ones. U.S. Cyber Command has been involved in assessment.

Impact:
Potential exposure of sensitive tactical, personnel, logistics, or related data on a major military cloud platform. Operational friction while contained.

Source:
https://t.co/FxEnz2p1B0

Mitigation:
Official military response is not detailed publicly beyond the report of discovery and disruption. For organizations, this is a reminder of control-plane and cloud-management risks; apply least-privilege and rapid patching to management interfaces.

9. Exposed credential collections (~2 billion records from infostealer malware; related larger aggregate reports)
Incident:
Security researcher Jeremiah Fowler identified a publicly accessible, unencrypted, passwordless database holding an estimated ~2 billion credential records (emails, usernames, passwords, cookies, session tokens, device data, etc.). The structure is consistent with aggregation of data stolen by information-stealer malware. Access was later restricted after reporting. Separate reporting (e.g., Wired) noted additional large exposed collections, bringing combined figures into the multi-billion range. These are collections of previously stolen data rather than a single new company breach.

Impact:
Large volume of reusable credentials, session tokens, and related material available to attackers for credential stuffing, session hijacking, or targeted follow-on activity. Duplicates mean the unique-person count is lower than the record count.

Source(s):
Reports via ExpressVPN / Jeremiah Fowler and coverage in Wired, TechSpot, CNET, Malwarebytes, etc. (original researcher findings published around 24 November 2026).

Mitigation:
Enable and enforce multi-factor authentication everywhere possible. Prefer unique passwords or a password manager. Check Have I Been Pwned or similar services for your accounts and rotate any reused or exposed credentials. Session tokens can be invalidated by signing out everywhere or changing passwords. Run reputable malware scans on personal devices. No single “patch”, this is simply hygiene and monitoring that should be already done.

10. AI-agent-driven mass compromise campaigns (Italy ACN/CSIRT Italia and Switzerland NCSC)
Incident:
Italy’s CSIRT Italia (ACN) issued a critical bulletin (23 November 2026) documenting mass compromise campaigns using autonomous AI agents (frameworks including ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness, Red Team, and PentAGI). Agents identified misconfigurations and vulnerabilities, chained issues, and compromised large numbers of systems within hours, sometimes pivoting into internal networks. The bulletin listed 81 CVEs tied to the activity. Switzerland’s NCSC reported its first confirmed AI-agent attacks (including against critical-infrastructure operators), with most known cases resulting in compromise. These align with earlier warnings about tools like ARTEX.

Impact: 
Rapid, automated exploitation of exposed edge devices, firewalls, VPNs, routers, and similar systems. Speed and scale exceed typical human-driven attacks.

Source:
ACN / CSIRT Italia bulletin: https://t.co/VKC3g3uies  
Related coverage of Swiss NCSC statements.

Mitigation:
Prioritize patching of the listed CVEs and any internet-exposed management interfaces. Remove or strictly control remote access to management pages (prefer VPN + MFA). Change default or weak credentials. Isolate systems that cannot be patched quickly. Monitor for rapid scanning or unexpected authentication activity. ACN has indicated ongoing technical guidance.

Ransomware volume and OT/ICS items

Ransomware leak-site activity remains high in November 2026 (one of the busiest periods tracked), with groups such as Qilin, The Gentlemen, and newer actors like N0N particularly active. These often leverage the same classes of initial-access flaws (exposed RDP/VPN, unpatched edge devices, stolen credentials) described above. Older flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers (CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, CVE-2025-41450) were also added to CISA KEV in late November after exploitation reports; apply available fixes and segment the networks.

Practical takeaway:
The most effective steps remain the basics done promptly, patch internet-facing and management systems, restrict exposure of installers/admin interfaces, enforce MFA, monitor for anomalous activity, and review logs on high-value assets. 
Many of the issues above have vendor fixes already available; the window between disclosure/KEV addition and widespread exploitation continues to shrink. 

For any specific system you run, check the vendor advisory and CISA KEV entry directly. 

This overview is based on public information available on 27 November 2026 and will evolve as new details emerge.

You closed the ticket, told your boss Drupal was handled, and went home, while your site sat in a stranger's pocket serving its homepage with a smile. CVE-2026-136716 hits sites that already got the first fix, damn.

HALF INSTALLED, FULLY OWNED
The first bug, CVE-2026-132165, got patched November 18. On November 25 Drupal said certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states stayed open to takeover anyway, production included, and it's being exploited in the wild. From the frying pan into the fire, and the fire has an instaler page.

THE DASHBOARD IS A LIAR
What pisses me off is that nothing in the UI tells you if you're in that state, and a compromised site may no longer be in it. Your dashboard is a quizmaster reading scores to an empty table, cheerful and useless as hell.

THE PRESS OFFICE
Picture the meeting: we are monitoring the situation. Translation: shit is on fire. No further details yet, so the damn guesing game lands on you.

THE CLEANUP
Upgrade to 10.6.23, 11.3.23 or 11.4.14, then run update.php. Can't yet? Block /core/install.php. Read the user 1 logs twice, because the first pass is when you badly want to believe it's fine. 10.5 and earlier, and 11.2 and earlier, get no fixes, tough shit.

One bug, one patch, one bullshit sense of closure, and a week later the sequel. Assume the goddamn thing was popped until your own logs argue otherwise.

Two critical flaws in PHP's core memory management & error-handling engine expose servers to full Remote Code Execution (RCE) and silent memory disclosure—regardless of how secure your application code is.

4 Confirmed Attack Chains:
1️⃣ OOM Corruption (mod_php): Unauthenticated RCE via crafted multipart POST requests before app code even runs.
2️⃣ Stale Global State (PHP 8.5): Use-after-free triggered via fatal_error_backtraces across requests.
3️⃣ Stale Session State (mod_php & PHP-FPM): Use-after-free via session.upload_progress after fatal errors.
4️⃣ Memory Disclosure: Arbitrary server memory reads leaking session tokens, DB credentials & API keys.

Immediate Action:
Upgrade immediately to patched versions:
• PHP 8.2 ➡️ 8.2.35
• PHP 8.3 ➡️ 8.3.36
• PHP 8.4 ➡️ 8.4.27
• PHP 8.5 ➡️ 8.5.12

19 years of BitLocker lockout just collapsed to 20 days because of a $1 motherboard flash chip.

Firmware TPMs on modern laptops store failed PIN counts on external SPI flash. TPM 2.0 Dictionary Attack Protection enforces a 32-try limit followed by one guess every 10 minutes, relying on a JEDEC counter called RPMC inside that flash chip to stop state rollbacks.

 At ACM CCS 2026, researchers broke that lock on both sides.
On Winbond RPMC flash (25R and 74M chips), a 1-second voltage glitch leaks the HMAC signing key straight out of the chip. Any laptop using that flash, Intel or AMD, now accepts forged counter values and rolls back its failed-attempt state.

On AMD fTPM (CVE-2026-43613), the firmware skips verifying whether the counter ever incremented. A custom interposer sitting between the CPU and SPI flash blocks counter updates with zero glitching.

 Measured worst-case brute-force results on locked laptops:
  * 4-digit Windows Hello PIN: 69 days down to 40 hours
  * 6-digit BitLocker startup PIN: 19 years down to 20 days

Winbond has no patch timeline because fixing the leak takes new silicon. AMD published AMD-SB-7079 with firmware fixes rolling out from November 2026 through February 2027.

Researchers used a flash-chip interposer to bypass TPM lockout and guess Hello and BitLocker PINs in lab tests; AMD tracks CVE-2026-43613 (CVSS 5.1). Check devices for tampering; lengthen PINs.

Your PC has a mechanism that remembers every incorrect PIN attempt and eventually locks you out

Researchers at TU Berlin found a way to make that mechanism forget

Their attack, called Hello Again, targets the Replay Protected Monotonic Counters (RPMC) used to protect security state stored in motherboard flash memory

The TPM relies on this state to remember failed authentication attempts and prevent brute-force guessing

The researchers found two ways to undermine that protection:

On affected AMD systems, they intercepted communication between the processor and flash chip, suppressing counter updates while making the processor believe they succeeded
On systems using vulnerable Winbond flash chips, voltage glitching exposed a cryptographic key that allowed the researchers to forge counter values

With the lockout state repeatedly reset, they could automate PIN guesses without the normal security delays

Their laboratory demonstrations included:

A four-digit Windows Hello PIN found in 57 minutes, with a worst-case estimated search time of 40 hours instead of 69 days
A six-digit BitLocker startup PIN found in under seven minutes, with a worst-case estimate of 20 days instead of 19 years

The attack required physical access, specialised hardware and vulnerable hardware configurations

It also affects different platforms for different reasons

AMD assigned its firmware issue CVE-2026-43613 and is planning firmware fixes extending into February 2027

Intel says the research did not demonstrate a vulnerability in Intel components; the tested Intel system depended on a flaw in its third-party Winbond flash chip

For now, researchers recommend using longer PINs, adding at least two digits where possible

The deeper security lesson is that a PIN's strength depends not only on how difficult it is to guess, but also on whether the hardware enforcing guess limits can be trusted

The custom exploit reportedly worked against default PHP/Apache configurations: a multipart POST with more than 1,000 fields and excessive header lines exhausted PHP’s memory limit, while a second request on the same keep-alive connection used residual session state to leak memory and invoke `system`. The campaign targeted 595 unique IPs across 57 countries; 404 hosts were assessed as compromised, with approximately 290,000 files (9.5 GB) collected. Exploitation and collection were organized through a job-based C2 and an AI-agent system: a custom queue dispatched 39 workers backed by two self-hosted DeepSeek endpoints. The evidence indicates human-directed, AI-assisted operations; complete autonomous execution was not established.

Post-compromise activity included reverse shells, SSH-key installation, periodic beacons, token-protected PHP webshells, cron persistence, and localhost-only Dropbear tunnels. Collection scripts inventoried hosts, searched repositories for secrets, gathered database backups and application data, and harvested cloud credentials, OAuth tokens, session files, and source code. A separate financial-fraud effort reached withdrawal and account-takeover capabilities, but no cryptocurrency theft was confirmed; an unauthenticated Redis instance did yield about 3.3 million user records.

Gorbag is a Russia-aligned cyberespionage group that has targeted Ukrainian organizations near the border since at least February 2025. Its targets include transportation and logistics, defense, law enforcement, government, and city councils. Spearphishing emails have used themes such as taxes, fines, military conscription, and drone procurement, and were sometimes sent from compromised Ukrainian government accounts.

A `Workbook_Open` VBA routine decoded Base64-encoded payloads stored in spreadsheet cells, wrote them to `%ProgramData%`, and executed them. The payloads included Prime ReverseShell, a PowerShell reverse shell based on the open-source PSSW100AVB project and packaged with PS2EXE. It delays execution by two or eight minutes and obscures its command-and-control address among decoy IP addresses.

The archives display a decoy PDF while placing a shortcut in the Windows Startup folder. At each logon, the shortcut runs a PowerShell loader that decrypts and executes the payload.

The group also uses BeautyStealer, a custom C++ information stealer tracked from versions 0.9 to 2.0. It collects browser cookies, saved passwords, profile data, and OpenVPN configurations; version 1.1 added collection of documents, KeePass databases, and Java keystores. Its strings have used XOR and later RC4 encryption, while exfiltration shifted from a Telegram bot to HTTPS POST requests to a custom FastAPI server. The malware deletes itself after execution.

Однако, учитывая постоянный доступ злоумышленника к устройствам Check Point, они считают, что кампания остается активной.

По данным GreyNoise, 22 организации-жертвы расположены в 17 странах, среди которых госучреждения, поставщики финансовых услуг, а также компании энергетического, транспортного, горнодобывающего и производственного секторов.

Уязвимость связана с обходом аутентификации в Check Point SmartConsole, которая позволяет злоумышленникам получить токен для входа в приложение и пройти аутентификацию с правами администратора.

В свою очередь, Check Point предупредила о ней еще в июле, обозначив ее как активно используемую 0-day.

Исследователи также зафиксировали попытки использования CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole) и CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF).

26 октября злоумышленник провел операцию по массовому управлению сертификатами на всех 24 скомпрометированных серверах Check Point, которая завершилась неудачей, но зато помогла GreyNoise идентифицировать жертв.

Исследователи пришли к выводу, что GT13 использовала инструмент нападения на основе ИИ, основываясь на поведении, наблюдаемой автоматизации и специально разработанных инструментах, однако использование ИИ в этой кампании остается неподтвержденным.

Учитывая, что кампания все еще может быть активной, GreyNoise поделилась IOCs, которые могут помочь выявить дополнительные вторжения или заблокировать будущие попытки.

Таким образом, эта уязвимость и доступные средства защиты не являются новыми. Злоумышленники также использовали адаптированный общедоступный модуль Metasploit для CVE-2026-16232, поэтому метод эксплуатации уже был известен ранее.

В общем, будем следить.

Keywords: export controls · Black Friday rebound · $41 billion pharma deal · MCP mandate · privacy auction · NFS2ROOT

Compute now needs a licence to cross some borders. AI stocks did not wait. Neither, if a bankruptcy auction goes ahead, would millions of private chatbot conversations.

On Thursday the Financial Times reported that Nvidia had told partners to pause AI-server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, after a new U.S. export rule took effect last week. On Friday’s short post-Thanksgiving session, the Nasdaq rose 2.31%, led by memory stocks, though Nvidia itself gained only 0.8%. The same week: Sanofi’s $41 billion purchase of Insmed, its largest deal in two decades; Google’s requirement that AI agents use official MCP servers or the Workspace CLI from 1 February 2027; a move by 42 attorneys general to stop https://t.co/YgSClWu149 auctioning more than 21 million private chats; and CVE-2026-99362, a 12-year-old Linux NFS flaw rated 9.8, with no confirmed use in the wild yet.

1. Nvidia pauses AI-server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

On 26 November 2026, the Financial Times, citing three people familiar with the matter, reported that Nvidia had told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. Partners including Dell and Supermicro had told buyers in those four countries that the orders would not be allowed to ship. It was unclear whether the halt would be temporary while the companies work out how to comply. Nvidia declined to comment; Dell and Supermicro did not respond. This follows that reporting, not an official company confirmation.

The background is an interim final rule from the U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security. BIS released it on 16 November; it became effective on 19 November, when published in the Federal Register. A licence is now required to export, reexport or transfer advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil — five destinations BIS describes as presenting a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The reported shipment pause covers the four Southeast Asian countries, not Brazil. Separately, any data centre already providing a significant volume of computing power to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, Macau or Country Group D:5, and that wishes to continue must obtain a licence within 90 days of the effective date. The aim is to close a path in which restricted entities rent advanced U.S. chips remotely through third-country data centres. The FT added that much of the region’s recent data-centre investment is in jeopardy, especially in Malaysia and Indonesia.

2. AI stocks rebound in a Black Friday half-day session — with a few figures that need care

U.S. markets were open for a shortened session on Friday, 27 November, the day after Thanksgiving, and finished higher, led by chip and other AI-linked names. Reuters put the official closes at: Nasdaq Composite up 543.70 points, or 2.31%, to 24,129.50; S&P 500 up 114.71 points, or 1.60%, to 7,297.49; Dow Jones Industrial Average up 591.99 points, or 1.18%, to 50,774.94. On Tuesday, 24 November 2026 — not Monday — Sanofi announced an agreement to acquire Insmed, a U.S. biopharmaceutical company, for $175 per share in cash, a total equity value of about $41.0 billion, or €37.6 billion. 4. Google requires AI agents to use Workspace MCP or the CLI from 1 February 2027

Also on Tuesday, 24 November, Google made eight official hosted Google Workspace MCP servers generally available — Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks, with Keep described as coming soon — along with the official Workspace CLI, gwscli, and published a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum. Google’s developer tools reference, updated on 27 November, also lists a People API MCP server as generally available, a ninth official server not listed in the 24 November product blog.

Technical enforcement begins on 1 February 2027. From that date, AI agents or similar access tools must use Google’s Workspace MCP servers or the Workspace CLI to access Workspace data, rather than calling Workspace REST APIs directly. Agents that keep calling the REST APIs directly are limited to Standard Tier quotas, regardless of paid tier. The Addendum’s first clause states the same requirement: a “GWS Access Tool” that is, or is driven by, an AI agent, an AI harness, or an AI model must use a Google MCP, and may not be disguised to avoid that classification.

What those servers can actually do is still settling, and should not be treated as a fixed menu. Early write-ups, including Flavio Copes on 26 November, reported that the public Gmail MCP server could search, read, manage labels and create drafts, while send, reply, forward and edit-draft tools were listed as partner-only. A 27 November independent probe found unauthenticated tools/list calls to the live Gmail endpoint flip-flopped that day: 18 of 30 requests returned 23 tools, and 12 returned 30, including send_message, reply, forward and update_draft. Google’s 27 November tools reference now documents 30 Gmail tools on the primary /mcp/v1 endpoint and 25 on /mcp/v1self; the Gmail setup guide describes sending, replying and forwarding as available, with user confirmation through form elicitation on the primary endpoint. Official pages were still being updated around launch; developers should not assume a single tools/list response is stable.

On Tuesday, 24 November, California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced that a bipartisan coalition of 42 attorneys general — 41 states and the District of Columbia, not 42 states — had objected in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware to https://t.co/YgSClWu149’s plan to auction its platform and the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including more than 2.1 million registered to minors, plus personal data such as IP addresses. (The same California release once quotes Bonta as saying “45 attorneys general”; the formal count in the release and the state list is 42, used here.) The auction is set for 1 December 2026; a sale hearing is set for 3 and 4 December.

The only disclosed bidder so far, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was formed in Delaware on 13 November and selected the next day as the stalking-horse bidder. Disney has a separate $20 million non-exclusive licence for https://t.co/YgSClWu149 technology that, per reporting and court notices, does not include user chats; that transaction has not received final court approval, and a similar coalition has already objected to it.

6. NFS2ROOT: a 12-year-old Linux NFS flaw, CVE-2026-99362, rated 9.8

A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s NFS server was assigned CVE-2026-99362 on 19 November 2026 and has been called NFS2ROOT. The European Union Vulnerability Database lists a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). Public reporting describes a heap buffer overflow in the in-kernel NFS server (nfsd) when handling NFSv4.1 or NFSv4.2 sessions. The weakness has been present since Linux 3.16, released in March 2014 — about 12 years.

At a high level, an unauthenticated attacker who can reach a vulnerable server may be able to obtain root privileges, with no user interaction required. This briefing does not describe how. OpenSec has published a video demonstration of a remote root shell and said the exploit remains private. As of BleepingComputer’s 27 November report, there were no reports of exploitation in the wild. The flaw was found independently by Jérémy Jean of France’s ANSSI, who submitted a fix in August, and by OpenSec, which reported it to maintainers in September. Patched versions listed by CSO, and in the EU vulnerability record, include 5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 and 7.4-rc1.

Explainer: What is MCP, and why is Google tightening this channel?

MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard announced by Anthropic on 25 November 2024 to unify how AI models connect to external tools and data. Before MCP, each model typically needed a custom connector for each tool — N models times M tools. MCP standardises that interface.

The protocol groups a server’s capabilities into three primitives: Resources (readable data), Prompts (reusable templates) and Tools (actions the model can invoke). Routing Workspace access through Google’s official MCP servers means the operator of the server also decides what an agent may do. High-risk actions can be gated or made to require confirmation; quotas and billing sit with Google.

Researchers have already warned that this convenience brings a new attack surface: a tool’s text description can be seeded with hidden instructions (tool poisoning), leading a model to take unauthorised actions; content retrieved through a tool can also carry indirect prompt injection. Google’s mandate pulls this channel back under the platform’s hand.

Anchor papers: Hou, X. et al. (2025). “Model Context Protocol (MCP): Landscape, Security Threats, and Future Research Directions.” arXiv:2503.23278. Gaire, S. et al. (2025). “Systematization of Knowledge: Security and Safety in the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem.” arXiv:2512.08290.

新知识科普：MCP是什么？为何Google要收紧这条通道？

MCP（Model Context Protocol，模型上下文协议）是Anthropic于2024年11月25日公布的开放标准，用以统一AI模型接驳外部工具与数据的方式。在此之前，每个模型要接每个工具，往往都要各自编写接驳器——N个模型乘M个工具。MCP把这套接口标准化。

协议把服务器能力分成三种原语：Resources（只读数据）、Prompts（可复用提示模板）和Tools（可执行的操作）。把Workspace接驳点收归Google官方MCP服务器，意味着谁控制服务器，谁就决定代理能做什么：高风险操作可以被关上或改为需要确认，配额与计费也由Google掌握。

学术界已经提醒，这种便利伴随着新的攻击面：工具的文字描述可被植入隐藏指令（工具投毒），使模型执行未授权操作；经工具取回的外部内容，也可能夹带间接提示注入。Google的强制令，正是把这条通道收回到平台之手。

The report describes misuse of ARTEX, an LLM-powered penetration-testing framework, across several campaigns. Reported activity includes attacks against South Korean financial organizations, Japanese companies, IT and software vendors, and financial-sector targets. The operators remain unknown in the Korean and Japanese cases; the report treats them as separate intrusions and does not infer shared attribution from overlapping infrastructure. Storm-0940 activity involved password spraying and abuse of ConnectWise Cloud Backup-related access. Storm-3358 activity involved financial-sector targeting and infrastructure associated with WISP. Other reported tools include vshell and AdaptixC2.

Common behaviors include rapid reconnaissance of web and API surfaces; enumeration of distinct customer or application records; probing authentication, SSO, OAuth, and application endpoints; and password spraying with rotating user agents. Other patterns include repeated requests with altered headers or tokens, SSRF attempts using redirecting URLs to reach internal or metadata addresses, and downloading exposed configuration or backup files. Cloud activity includes exposed-secret use, service-principal sign-ins, OAuth credential addition, and credential discovery across AWS services. The report also describes upload-then-execute behavior and self-correcting API retries, including retries after HTTP 422 responses.

The detection approach prioritizes behavior over framework-specific strings, which can be changed or generated by the model. Proposed rules correlate sequences such as multiple distinct reconnaissance requests within a short window, high-volume record access, and file uploads followed by execution. ARTEX-specific headers, user agents, webshell keys, response markers, domains, and IP addresses are treated as supporting indicators; shared infrastructure and generic user agents require caution. Reported Windows artifacts include files named in an intent-ID/purpose/extension format and paths under `C:\Windows\Temp` or `C:\ProgramData`; these are described as renameable indicators rather than durable detections.

The report recommends correlating network telemetry with identity and cloud logs. The evidence base distinguishes three tiers of AI-discovered vulnerability claims, and they carry different confidence levels.

The first tier — software and library vulnerabilities — is well-documented. Google GTIG tracked 2,076 AI-related CVEs between January 2025 and August 2026, with more than 1,500 in 2026 alone, roughly half affecting AI orchestration frameworks [Source: SecurityWeek / Google GTIG, Sep 30, 2026]. One named example, CVE-2026-1731, was an unauthenticated OS command injection flaw in BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access discovered autonomously by the Hacktron AI research agent; one threat cluster exploited it within four days of public disclosure, and five more followed within seven days [Source: SecurityWeek / Google GTIG, Sep 30, 2026]. The Axios reporting on early testing of new frontier models describes Cisco and Zscaler using them internally to "chain together vulnerabilities to build an exploit chain" — the shift from single-bug discovery to multi-step attack path construction [Source: Axios, Apr 21, 2026].

The second tier — kernel and root-access flaws — is documented at one confirmed instance. Between April 29 and May 13, 2026, three publicly disclosed flaws gave local users a path to root access across major Linux distributions. Microsoft confirmed that AI found the "Copy Fail" vulnerability among them, and assessed that "the other two fit the same broader pattern, suggesting that AI will increase the pace at which serious vulnerability classes are discovered" [Source: Microsoft MDDR, Oct 9, 2026]. Kernel-level access is the layer immediately above hardware — it controls hardware, memory, and system processes. An attacker who compromises the kernel gains, in Microsoft's words, "total dominion over the system." This is the closest documented open-source analogue to what Altman describes as "hardware-level, insane stuff."

The third tier — structurally unpatchable hardware vulnerabilities, Altman's specific claim — is where open-source evidence runs thin. The Mother Jones piece notes that a PHP vulnerability type had been "noted decades ago, but the flaw had been considered too difficult to exploit and was largely forgotten until August [2026], when researchers using new models found a way to exploit it" [Source: Mother Jones, Oct 21, 2026]. This describes a class of vulnerability where the flaw was known but assumed to be beyond exploitation — AI changed the feasibility calculation, not the patching requirement. That is distinct from hardware bugs that physically cannot be patched. Altman's statement remains the primary public evidence for the hardware-unpatchable category; no independent technical source corroborates it with specifics in the collected evidence. 1/6

An issue was discovered in HAProxy 3.3.0 through 3.4.4 and in 3.5-dev1 through 3.5-dev5. Exploitation requires an HTTP/3 frontend: HAProxy must be built with QUIC support and configured with a QUIC bind listener, and the affected traffic must reach a backend over HTTP/1.1 using chunked transfer coding on a reused connection. Under those conditions, when an HTTP/3 request carries no Content-Length header, the HTTP/3 multiplexer credits the length declared in a DATA frame header to the stream endpoint's known-input-payload estimate at the moment the frame header is decoded, before the payload has been received, and that declared length is emitted verbatim as the HTTP/1.1 chunk size. A remote unauthenticated client that declares more payload than it delivers and then ends the stream causes HAProxy to announce a chunk larger than the bytes it writes and to return the connection to the idle pool in a desynchronized state. The result is potential HTTP request smuggling on reused backend connections: an attacker can place a request past a frontend rule such as a path-based http-request deny, so that the smuggled request is never seen by HAProxy's HTTP analysis, and can cause concurrent clients' requests, including their request lines and Authorization headers, to be consumed as the attacker's request body and lost. Exploitation is not deterministic; it depends on a race with backend connection pooling, succeeding in a majority of but not all trials during testing, and can be retried freely. The mechanism was introduced in 3.3-dev10; releases 3.2.x and earlier are unaffected.

The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::process request in libnetutil/massdns.cc that frees still-referenced requests when rescheduling after DNS server disconnects. Attackers answering for at least two configured DNS servers can force a disconnect and send a precisely timed response to crash the scan, possibly enabling code execution.

The MCUmgr SMP client matched an incoming response to a pending command in smp client response discover() (subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp client/src/client.c) using only the 8-bit sequence number and the operation. It did not check the transport the response arrived on, or the group and command ID. smp process request packet() hands every MGMT OP READ RSP/MGMT OP WRITE RSP packet received on any SMP transport to smp client single response(), so a response from any SMP peer could complete any pending client command.

On a device that is both an SMP server (for example over Bluetooth LE or UDP) and an SMP client (CONFIG SMP CLIENT, for example using img mgmt client to update a companion MCU over UART), a peer on the server transport can send up to 256 forged response packets while a client operation is pending and have one of them accepted as the reply from the managed device. Non-matching responses are dropped silently. The response path bypasses the server command handlers, so restricting which server groups a peer may use does not prevent it.

The attacker can forge the results of client operations. For example, a forged image-upload offset makes img mgmt client upload() report success after only part of the image was sent, a forged image-state response can report arbitrary versions or flags, and any pending command can be forced to fail. No memory corruption results: the response callbacks bound-check the decoded data. The target's own image validation limits the result to failed or suppressed updates and disrupted management operations. The fix restricts matching to commands sent on the same transport with the same group and command ID. Responses from a different peer on the same transport are still not distinguished.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::handle write in libnetutil/massdns.cc that dereferences freed request objects after writes complete. Attackers controlling or on-path to a DNS server can send timed DNS responses with forged ICMP port-unreachable messages to crash scans, disclose memory, or hijack execution.
